prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Reordering sign-in after adoption (sign_in, reorder) was helpful (+7.0%), though the measured lift was less than predicted (+15.0%).
Streamlining path selection copy (choose_path, copy) significantly hurt performance (-4.7%), contrary to the predicted +5.0% gain.
Grid selection layouts (adoption, layout) showed no clear effect.
Background notifications upon completion (finish, notification) showed no clear effect.
Estimated wait times and desktop alerts (home, wait_info) showed no clear effect.
Predictions were consistently too optimistic across all tested changes.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, layout: +2.7% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, copy: -4.7% over 1 test(s)
- finish, notification: +5.4% over 1 test(s)
- home, wait_info: -0.5% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: +7.0% over 1 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 78.2%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 19.1%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Pet Quick Guide Screen: Insert a new quick guide screen before home_intro that clearly illustrates how to summon, control, and hide the desktop pet after setup. (why: Conversion drops at finish (64.8%) and multiple support emails expressed confusion about controlling, hiding, or talking to the pet post-onboarding.)
1: [choose_path, new_flow] Interactive Onboarding Story Arc: Rebuild the story screen into an interactive choice flow with companion cards to engage users before path selection. (why: Choose path has a high mean duration of 514s and 76.2% conversion, showing early user hesitation or distraction.)
2: [sign_in, reorder] Sign-In Post Adoption Certificate Flow: Move sign-in to take place immediately following adoption_certificate so pet creation details are explicitly bound to the account prior to waiting. (why: Sign-in had 8 support emails concerning pets missing or reset after signing in again, indicating confusion over when pet state gets linked.)
3: [home, hint] Desktop Waiting Hint and Carousel: Add an explicit status hint and tip carousel to the waiting screen explaining what the app is setting up on the desktop. (why: Home target step (waiting screen) has a very high mean time (2336s) and 81.3% conversion, with support mails reporting pets failing to appear on desktop.)
4: [finish, copy] Clear First Desktop Interaction Copy: Update the headline, body, and call-to-action on home_intro to clearly instruct users where to find their pet on screen. (why: 3 support tickets reported post-onboarding confusion on how to interact or locate the pet on desktop.)
5: [sign_in, notification] Account Sync Safeguard Hint: Display an explicit sync notification hint and badge on the sign-in screen assuring users that pet progress will be saved. (why: 8 support emails cited lost or reset pets after re-authenticating.)
6: [home, wait_info] Pet Desktop Ready Status Bar: Enable show_progress and add a desktop loading progress component to the waiting screen. (why: Users experience long wait times (mean 2336s) on the waiting screen and report issues where the app stalls or pet fails to show up.)

scores.note: Finish loses 35.2% of users and support reports confusion, but creating a new screen has high implementation cost.
Rebuilding flow is costly and complex copy/flow changes previously hurt performance.
Reordering sign_in previously yielded +7.0% lift, directly matching strong user support evidence.
Home step has high wait time and user issues, though info hints typically offer modest improvements.
Simple copy change addressing finish step drop-off is cheap to configure.
Strong support evidence for sign_in concerns; low cost notification/badge updates.
Home wait info changes previously showed no clear positive effect (-0.5%).
